property_summary: MinSum can be set despite initialized being true.
After a call to Collect, MinSum remains at its initial default zero in the original, whereas in the mutant it can be non-zero if SetMinSum was called before.

After any sequence of calls including Collect, MinSum must remain unchanged from its last explicit SetMinSum call; the mutant violates this by allowing SetMinSum to modify MinSum even after initialization.
After initialization, the value of MinSum can never be changed, but the mutant allows SetMinSum to modify it at any time.
After initialization and at least one call to Collect, MinSum must always stay at its current value; the mutant allows SetMinSum to reset it after initialization.
After initialization, MinSum must never be modified by any subsequent call to SetMinSum, but the buggy version always updates it on every SetMinSum call.
After initialization, calling SetMinSum must not change MinSum, but the buggy version always updates it.
SetMinSum should revert when called while the nonReentrant lock is held, but in M it succeeds because the lock is never set.
A reentrant call to Put via the fallback during the Collect external call cannot succeed in P because the nonReentrant modifier prevents reentry, but succeeds in M.
The nonReentrant modifier should prevent a call executed during Collect from changing the lock state, so that a reentrant call to SetMinSum reverts.

property_summary: After any call to Collect, MinSum remains unchanged from its prior value.
While the nonReentrant lock is engaged, any call to SetMinSum must revert.
MinSum should be immutable after initialization, but the buggy modifier allows SetMinSum to be called reentrantly from Collect, changing MinSum.
After initialization, MinSum must never change, but the buggy nonReentrant_ modifier allows SetMinSum to be called during execution of Collect, altering MinSum.

After initialization, MinSum must remain constant through Collect, but the buggy nonReentrant modifier allows a reentrant call to SetMinSum via a malicious callee, changing MinSum during Collect execution.
After a call to Collect completes, MinSum must remain unchanged; the buggy nonReentrant modifier allows a reentrant call to SetMinSum from within Collect's external call, altering MinSum.

The nonReentrant_ modifier must prevent reentrant calls to SetMinSum so that MinSum can be set at most once; the buggy modifier allows a reentrant call to re-enter and change MinSum again, violating the invariant that MinSum never changes after its first setting.

After an external call to SetMinSum returns, the stored MinSum remains unchanged relative to its value immediately before the call, regardless of any reentrant callback from a callee; the bug allows a reentrant call to modify MinSum again.

After the first successful call to SetMinSum, the stored MinSum value remains immutable for any subsequent external call that returns successfully; the buggy nonReentrant_ allows a re-entrant call to alter MinSum again.
After any successful external call chain finishes, MinSum equals its value from before the call, demonstrating immutability once initialized; the bug allows a reentrant call to change MinSum.
After initialization, any call to SetMinSum must revert because the nonReentrant modifier is locked; the buggy modifier allows a successful re-entrant call to change MinSum.
SetLogFile should revert when the contract is already initialized.
Calling SetLogFile must always revert when the contract is already locked (reentrancy guard active); the buggy version allows the call to succeed in that state.

When called while `locked_` is true (reentrancy call), `SetLogFile` must always revert; the buggy version allows a nested call to succeed, making `intitalized` stay false and `SetLogFile` to change state, observable via a subsequent `Initialized` call and `MinSum` getter.

In any reentrant call (locked_ == true) initiated during execution of a nonReentrant_ function, calling SetLogFile must revert; the mutant allows it to succeed, changing the Log address while locked, which is observable via the public getter after the call.
For any call sequence, if SetLogFile is called inside a reentrant call (when locked_ is true), it must revert; the mutant allows it to succeed, changing Log which is observable via the public getter.

For any sequence where SetLogFile is called after a nonReentrant function re-enters via a crafted callee, the reference always reverts on the inner SetLogFile call, while the buggy version allows it to succeed, changing Log which is then observable via the public getter.

After a successful call to SetLogFile, the Log state variable must be updated to the provided address; the buggy version fails to update Log, so retrieving the Log address via the auto-generated getter returns a different (unchanged) address.

After SetLogFile is called with any address, subsequent calls to a payable fallback (or Put) that trigger Log.AddMessage must not revert; the buggy version leaves Log as the zero address, so Log.AddMessage will revert due to call to address 0.

After SetLogFile is called, the Log address getter matches the argument supplied; the buggy version leaves Log uninitialized, so the getter returns address(0) instead, detectable by comparing the returned address with the argument.

After a successful call to SetLogFile, calling the fallback (which calls Put and then Log.AddMessage) must not revert, regardless of the address given; the buggy version fails to update Log, causing a call to address(0) and a revert when Log.AddMessage is invoked.

After calling SetLogFile with any address, if the contract is uninitialized, the Log state variable must equal LogFile(_log); the buggy version sets it to LogFile(address(0)) instead, violating this invariant.
After SetLogFile is called when intitalized is false, the address returned by address(c.Log()) must equal the _log argument provided. The buggy version ignores _log and sets it to address(0).

After calling SetLogFile with address x while uninitialized, a subsequent Put call that should emit an event via Log must not revert; the buggy version sets Log to address(0), causing the AddMessage call inside Put to revert due to calling on address(0).
After SetLogFile is called before initialization, calling Put must not revert; the buggy version sets Log to address(0), which causes a revert on the subsequent AddMessage call inside Put.

After the first call to c.SetLogFile(...), a subsequent reentrant call to c.SetLogFile(...) should always revert because the nonReentrant_ modifier prevents reentry. The bug removes the lock, allowing the reentrant call to succeed.
